translations.idiomatic: Use tassels, reins, and scarlet overshoes.

sentences.zh: 禦馬鞍勒之製，有金、玉、水晶、金塗四等鬧裝，䩞鞢促結為坐龍，碾鈒鏤塵沙麵、平麵、窪麵、方團、寸節、卷荷校具，皆垂六鞘，金銀裹鞍橋、銜鐙，朱黃絲絛轡鞦，緋黃織繡或素園韉，衤蓋補用金銀線織或緋黃絁，鞭用紫竹，紅黃絲鞘，纓以紅、黃犛牛尾，金為鈌。

translations.literal: The design of imperial horse saddles and bridles had four grades of decorated fittings—gold, jade, crystal, and gold-plated—with 䩞鞢 fittings tied into seated-dragon forms, and chased and engraved fittings in dust-sand, flat, concave, square-round, inch-knot, and curled-lotus styles, all with six sheaths hanging down; saddle arches, bits, and stirrups were wrapped in gold and silver; vermilion and yellow silk cord reins and cruppers; scarlet and yellow woven or plain round saddle cloth; saddle covers and patches woven with gold and silver thread or scarlet and yellow silk; whips of purple bamboo with red and yellow silk sheaths; tassels of red and yellow yak tails; gold clasps.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial horse saddles and bridles had four grades of decorated fittings—gold, jade, crystal, and gold-plated—with 䩞鞢 fittings tied into seated-dragon forms. Other fittings were chased and engraved in dust-sand, flat, concave, square-round, inch-knot, and curled-lotus styles, all with six sheaths hanging down. Saddle arches, bits, and stirrups were wrapped in gold and silver; reins and cruppers were of vermilion and yellow silk cord; saddle cloth was scarlet and yellow woven or plain round cloth; covers and patches were woven with gold and silver thread or scarlet and yellow silk; whips were of purple bamboo with red and yellow silk sheaths; tassels were of red and yellow yak tails; and clasps were of gold.

sentences.zh: 每日，馬五匹供奉，鞍用玉及金塗，衤蓋補皆素。

translations.literal: Daily, five horses were on duty; saddles used jade and gold plating, and saddle covers and patches were all plain.
translations.idiomatic: Daily, five horses were on duty. Their saddles used jade and gold plating, and saddle covers and patches were all plain.

sentences.zh: 行幸則十四匹，加真金、水晶之飾。

translations.literal: On imperial tours there were fourteen horses, with added true gold and crystal ornamentation.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours there were fourteen horses, with added true gold and crystal ornamentation.

sentences.zh: 太宗至道二年詔：“先是，禦馬以織成帕覆鞍勒，今後以廣絹代之。”

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao under Emperor Taizong, an edict stated: "Previously, imperial horses used woven silk cloth to cover saddles and bridles; hereafter broad silk is to be used instead."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao, Emperor Taizong issued an edict: "Previously, imperial horses used woven silk cloth to cover saddles and bridles. Hereafter broad silk is to be used instead."

sentences.zh: 馬珂之製，銅麵，雕翎鼻拂，攀胸，上綴銅杏葉、紅絲拂。

translations.literal: The design of horse ornaments had a copper face, carved-feather nose duster, chest strap, with copper apricot-leaf ornaments and red silk tassels attached above.
translations.idiomatic: Horse ornaments had a copper face, carved-feather nose duster, and chest strap, with copper apricot-leaf ornaments and red silk tassels attached above.

sentences.zh: 又胸前及腹下，皆有攀，綴銅鈴；

translations.literal: On the chest and below the belly as well, there were straps with copper bells attached;
translations.idiomatic: On the chest and below the belly as well, there were straps with copper bells attached;

sentences.zh: 後有跋塵、錦包尾。

translations.literal: behind were tail dusters and brocade-wrapped tails.
translations.idiomatic: behind were tail dusters and brocade-wrapped tails.

sentences.zh: 獨鹵簿中金吾衛將軍導駕者，皆有之。

translations.literal: Only the Golden Guard generals leading the imperial carriage in the escort all had them.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Golden Guard generals leading the imperial carriage in the escort all had them.

sentences.zh: 甲騎具裝，甲，人鎧也；

translations.literal: Armored cavalry with full equipment: armor was human armor;
translations.idiomatic: Armored cavalry with full equipment: armor was human armor;

sentences.zh: 具裝，馬鎧也。

translations.literal: full equipment was horse armor.
translations.idiomatic: full equipment was horse armor.

sentences.zh: 甲以布為裏，黃絁表之，青綠畫為甲文，紅錦褖，青絁為下裙，絳韋為絡，金銅鈌，長短至膝。

translations.literal: The armor used cloth as lining, yellow silk as outer layer, green painted as armor pattern, red brocade border, green silk as lower skirt, dark red leather as netting, gold-copper clasps, length reaching the knee.
translations.idiomatic: The armor used cloth as lining and yellow silk as the outer layer, with green painted armor patterns, red brocade borders, green silk lower skirts, dark red leather netting, gold-copper clasps, and length reaching the knee.

sentences.zh: 前膺為人麵二，自背連膺，纏以錦螣蛇。

translations.literal: The front breast had two human faces, connected from back to breast and wrapped with brocade teng snakes.
translations.idiomatic: The front breast had two human faces, connected from back to breast and wrapped with brocade teng snakes.

sentences.zh: 具裝，如常馬甲，加珂拂於前膺及後鞦。

translations.literal: Full equipment was like ordinary horse armor, with ornaments and dusters added to the front breast and rear crupper.
translations.idiomatic: Full equipment was like ordinary horse armor, with ornaments and dusters added to the front breast and rear crupper.

sentences.zh: 球杖，金塗銀裹，以供奉官騎執之，分左右前導。

translations.literal: The ball mace was gold-plated and silver-wrapped, carried on horseback by palace attendants, leading left and right in front.
translations.idiomatic: The ball mace was gold-plated and silver-wrapped, carried on horseback by palace attendants who led left and right in front.

sentences.zh: 大禮，用百人，花腳襆頭、紫繡衤癸袍襖。

translations.literal: For great rites, one hundred men were used, wearing flowered-foot turbans and purple embroidered kui robes and jackets.
translations.idiomatic: For great rites, one hundred men were used, wearing flowered-foot turbans and purple embroidered kui robes and jackets.

sentences.zh: 常出，三十人，公服，皆騎導。

translations.literal: For ordinary outings, thirty men in official dress all rode as guides.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary outings, thirty men in official dress all rode as guides.

sentences.zh: 雞竿，附竿為雞形，金飾，首銜絳幡，承以彩盤，維以絳索，揭以長竿。

translations.literal: The golden rooster pole had a rooster shape attached to the pole, with gold ornamentation; its head held a crimson pennant, supported on a colored tray, bound with crimson cord, and raised on a long pole.
translations.idiomatic: The golden rooster pole had a rooster shape attached to the pole with gold ornamentation. Its head held a crimson pennant, supported on a colored tray, bound with crimson cord, and raised on a long pole.

sentences.zh: 募衛士先登，爭得雞者，官給以纈襖子；

translations.literal: Recruited guards raced to climb first; whoever won the rooster was given a variegated jacket by the court;
translations.idiomatic: Recruited guards raced to climb first. Whoever won the rooster was given a variegated jacket by the court;

sentences.zh: 或取絳幡而已。

translations.literal: or they took only the crimson pennant.
translations.idiomatic: or they took only the crimson pennant.

sentences.zh: 大禮畢，麗正門肆赦則設之。

translations.literal: When great rites ended and amnesty was proclaimed at Lizheng Gate, it was set up.
translations.idiomatic: When great rites ended and amnesty was proclaimed at Lizheng Gate, it was set up.

sentences.zh: 其義則雞為巽神，巽主號令，故宣號令則象之。

translations.literal: The meaning was that the rooster is the deity of Xun, and Xun governs commands; therefore proclaiming commands was symbolized by it.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning was that the rooster is the deity of Xun, and Xun governs commands. Therefore proclaiming commands was symbolized by it.

sentences.zh: 陽用事則雞鳴，故布宣陽澤則象之。

translations.literal: When yang holds sway the rooster crows; therefore spreading yang bounty was symbolized by it.
translations.idiomatic: When yang holds sway the rooster crows. Therefore spreading yang bounty was symbolized by it.

sentences.zh: 一曰“天雞星動為有赦”，故王者以天雞為度。

translations.literal: One explanation says "when the Heavenly Rooster star moves there is amnesty"; therefore sovereigns took the heavenly rooster as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: One explanation says "when the Heavenly Rooster star moves there is amnesty." Therefore sovereigns took the heavenly rooster as their measure.

sentences.zh: 金雞事，六朝已有之，或謂起於西京。

translations.literal: The golden rooster ceremony already existed in the Six Dynasties, or some say it began in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The golden rooster ceremony already existed in the Six Dynasties, or some say it began in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，則自紹興十三年始也。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, it began only in the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing, it began only in the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿巾服之製：金吾上將軍、將軍、六統軍、千牛、中郎將，服花腳襆頭、抹額、紫繡袍，佩牙刀，珂馬。

translations.literal: Regulations for headgear and dress in the grand imperial escort: Golden Guard senior generals, generals, the six army commanders, Thousand-Ox guards, and commandants of the palace guards wore flowered-foot turbans, forehead bands, and purple embroidered robes, carried court swords, and had ornamented horses.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for headgear and dress in the grand imperial escort: Golden Guard senior generals, generals, the six army commanders, Thousand-Ox guards, and commandants of the palace guards wore flowered-foot turbans, forehead bands, and purple embroidered robes, carried court swords, and rode ornamented horses.

sentences.zh: 諸衛大將軍、將軍、中郎將、折衝、果毅、散手翊衛，服平巾幘、紫繡袍、大口袴、錦螣蛇、銀帶，佩橫刀，執弓箭。

translations.literal: Generals, commandants, assault-resolute officers, and scattered-hand guards of the various guards wore plain cloth caps, purple embroidered robes, wide trousers, brocade teng snakes, and silver belts, carried horizontal swords, and held bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, commandants, assault-resolute officers, and scattered-hand guards of the various guards wore plain cloth caps, purple embroidered robes, wide trousers, brocade teng snakes, and silver belts, carried horizontal swords, and held bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍，服平巾幘、紫繡袍、大口袴、銀帶、靴靿，佩橫刀，執弓箭，珂馬。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox generals wore plain cloth caps, purple embroidered robes, wide trousers, silver belts, and boot tops, carried horizontal swords, held bows and arrows, and rode ornamented horses.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox generals wore plain cloth caps, purple embroidered robes, wide trousers, silver belts, and boot tops, carried horizontal swords, held bows and arrows, and rode ornamented horses.

sentences.zh: 千牛，服花腳襆頭、緋繡袍、抹額、大口袴、銀帶、靴靿。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox guards wore flowered-foot turbans, scarlet embroidered robes, forehead bands, wide trousers, silver belts, and boot tops.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Ox guards wore flowered-foot turbans, scarlet embroidered robes, forehead bands, wide trousers, silver belts, and boot tops.

sentences.zh: 前馬隊內折衝及執槊者，服錦帽、緋繡袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: Assault-resolute officers and spear-bearers within the front cavalry company wore brocade caps, scarlet embroidered robes, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Assault-resolute officers and spear-bearers within the front cavalry company wore brocade caps, scarlet embroidered robes, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉、六軍押仗，服襆頭、紫繡裲襠。

translations.literal: Gate guard captains and Six Armies guard officers wore turbans and purple embroidered doublets.
translations.idiomatic: Gate guard captains and Six Armies guard officers wore turbans and purple embroidered doublets.

sentences.zh: 隊正，服平巾幘、緋繡袍、大口袴。

translations.literal: Squad leaders wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, and wide trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leaders wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, and wide trousers.

sentences.zh: 諸衛主率都尉，引駕騎，持鈒隊內校尉、旅帥，執衛司殳仗暴槊，金吾十六騎，班劍、儀刀隊，親勳翊衛，執大角人，並服平巾幘、緋繡裲襠、大口袴，佩橫刀，執弓箭。

translations.literal: Commanders of the various guards, leading-cavalry escorts, captains and brigade chiefs within the inserted company, Guard Office shu-staff and bao-spear bearers, sixteen Golden Guard cavalry, patterned-sword and ceremonial-sword companies, personal guard attendants, and great-horn bearers all wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered doublets, and wide trousers, carried horizontal swords, and held bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of the various guards, leading-cavalry escorts, captains and brigade chiefs within the inserted company, Guard Office shu-staff and bao-spear bearers, sixteen Golden Guard cavalry, patterned-sword and ceremonial-sword companies, personal guard attendants, and great-horn bearers all wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered doublets, and wide trousers, carried horizontal swords, and held bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 金吾押牙，服金鵝帽、紫繡袍、銀帶，儀刀。

translations.literal: Golden Guard deputy commanders wore golden goose caps, purple embroidered robes, silver belts, and ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard deputy commanders wore golden goose caps, purple embroidered robes, silver belts, and ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 金吾持纛者，服烏紗帽、皂衣、袴、鞋襪。

translations.literal: Golden Guard standard bearers wore black gauze caps, black robes, trousers, shoes, and socks.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard standard bearers wore black gauze caps, black robes, trousers, shoes, and socks.

sentences.zh: 金吾押纛，服襆頭、皂繡衫、大口袴、銀帶、烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Golden Guard standard escorts wore turbans, black embroidered shirts, wide trousers, silver belts, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard standard escorts wore turbans, black embroidered shirts, wide trousers, silver belts, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 執金吾暴槊，服錦袍帽、臂鞲、銀帶、烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Golden Guard bao-spear bearers wore brocade robes and caps, arm guards, silver belts, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard bao-spear bearers wore brocade robes and caps, arm guards, silver belts, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 清遊隊、佽飛、執副仗槊，服甲騎具裝、錦臂韝，佩橫刀，執弓箭，白袴。

translations.literal: Clear Procession company, flying guards, and auxiliary guard spear bearers wore armored cavalry with full equipment, brocade arm guards, horizontal swords, bows and arrows, and white trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Clear Procession company, flying guards, and auxiliary guard spear bearers wore armored cavalry with full equipment, brocade arm guards, horizontal swords, bows and arrows, and white trousers.

sentences.zh: 朱雀隊執旗及執牙門旗，執絳引幡、黃麾幡者，並服緋繡衫、抹額、大口袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Vermilion Bird company flag bearers, gate banner bearers, crimson guide pennant bearers, and yellow command banner pennant bearers all wore scarlet embroidered shirts, forehead bands, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion Bird company flag bearers, gate banner bearers, crimson guide pennant bearers, and yellow command banner pennant bearers all wore scarlet embroidered shirts, forehead bands, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 執殳仗，前後步隊、真武隊執旗，前後部黃麾，執日月合璧等旗，青龍白虎隊、金吾細仗內執旗者，並服五色繡袍、抹額、行縢、銀帶；

translations.literal: Shu-staff bearers, front and rear foot companies, True Martial company flag bearers, front and rear yellow command banners, Sun-Moon Joined Discs flag bearers, Azure Dragon and White Tiger companies, and flag bearers within the Golden Guard detailed guard all wore five-colored embroidered robes, forehead bands, leg bindings, and silver belts;
translations.idiomatic: Shu-staff bearers, front and rear foot companies, True Martial company flag bearers, front and rear yellow command banners, Sun-Moon Joined Discs flag bearers, Azure Dragon and White Tiger companies, and flag bearers within the Golden Guard detailed guard all wore five-colored embroidered robes, forehead bands, leg bindings, and silver belts;

sentences.zh: 執白幹棒人，加銀褐捍腰。

translations.literal: white-shaft club bearers added silver-brown waist guards.
translations.idiomatic: white-shaft club bearers added silver-brown waist guards.

sentences.zh: 執龍旗及前馬隊內執旗人，服五色繡袍、銀帶、行縢、大口袴。

translations.literal: Dragon flag bearers and flag bearers within the front cavalry company wore five-colored embroidered robes, silver belts, leg bindings, and wide trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon flag bearers and flag bearers within the front cavalry company wore five-colored embroidered robes, silver belts, leg bindings, and wide trousers.

sentences.zh: 執弓箭、執龍旗副竿人，服錦帽、五色繡袍、大口袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bow and arrow bearers and dragon flag secondary pole bearers wore brocade caps, five-colored embroidered robes, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bow and arrow bearers and dragon flag secondary pole bearers wore brocade caps, five-colored embroidered robes, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 執弩、弓箭人，服錦帽、青繡袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: Crossbow and bow bearers wore brocade caps, green embroidered robes, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbow and bow bearers wore brocade caps, green embroidered robes, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 前後步隊人，服五色鍪甲、錦臂鞲、鞵襪、袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Front and rear foot company men wore five-colored helmet armor, brocade arm guards, shoes, socks, trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Front and rear foot company men wore five-colored helmet armor, brocade arm guards, shoes, socks, trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 朱雀隊內執弓箭、弩、槊，虞候佽飛，執長壽幢、寶輿法物人，並服平巾幘、緋繡袍、大口袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Within the Vermilion Bird company, bow, crossbow, and spear bearers, flying guards on patrol, and bearers of the Longevity banner-staff and precious carriage ritual objects all wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Vermilion Bird company, bow, crossbow, and spear bearers, flying guards on patrol, and bearers of the Longevity banner-staff and precious carriage ritual objects all wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 援寶，執絳麾、真武幢叉人，並服武弁、紫繡衫。

translations.literal: Those supporting the precious regalia, and bearers of crimson command banners and True Martial banner-staff forks, all wore military caps and purple embroidered shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Those supporting the precious regalia, and bearers of crimson command banners and True Martial banner-staff forks, all wore military caps and purple embroidered shirts.

sentences.zh: 持鈒隊，殿中黃麾、傘、扇、腰輿、香鐙、華蓋，指南、進賢等車駕士，相風、鍾漏等輿輿士，並服武弁、緋繡衫。

translations.literal: Inserted company, palace yellow command banners, umbrellas, fans, waist litters, incense tables, flower canopies, compass and Advance Worthy carriage attendants, wind-measuring and clock-water carriage attendants all wore military caps and scarlet embroidered shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Inserted company, palace yellow command banners, umbrellas, fans, waist litters, incense tables, flower canopies, compass and Advance Worthy carriage attendants, and wind-measuring and clock-water carriage attendants all wore military caps and scarlet embroidered shirts.

sentences.zh: 駕羊車童子，服垂耳髻、青頭{須巾}、青繡大袖衫、袴、勒帛、青耳履。

translations.literal: Sheep-carriage attendants wore hanging-ear topknots, green headcloths, green embroidered large-sleeve shirts, trousers, waist sashes, and green ear-shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep-carriage attendants wore hanging-ear topknots, green headcloths, green embroidered large-sleeve shirts, trousers, waist sashes, and green ear-shoes.

sentences.zh: 執引駕龍墀旗、六軍旗者，服錦帽、五色繡衫、錦臂鞲、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of the leading Dragon Court flags and Six Armies flags wore brocade caps, five-colored embroidered shirts, brocade arm guards, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of the leading Dragon Court flags and Six Armies flags wore brocade caps, five-colored embroidered shirts, brocade arm guards, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 引夾旗及執柯舒、鐙仗者，服帖金帽，餘同上。

translations.literal: Flanking flag bearers and ke-club and stirrup-staff bearers wore gold-inlaid caps; the rest was the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking flag bearers and ke-club and stirrup-staff bearers wore gold-inlaid caps. The rest was the same as above.

sentences.zh: 執花鳳、飛黃、吉利旗者，服銀褐繡衣、抹額、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of the Flower Phoenix, Flying Yellow, and Auspicious flags wore silver-brown embroidered garments, forehead bands, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of the Flower Phoenix, Flying Yellow, and Auspicious flags wore silver-brown embroidered garments, forehead bands, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 夾轂隊，服五色質鍪鎧、錦臂鞲、白行縢、紫帶、鞵襪。

translations.literal: Wheel-guarding company wore five-colored plain helmet armor, brocade arm guards, white leg bindings, purple belts, and shoes and socks.
translations.idiomatic: The wheel-guarding company wore five-colored plain helmet armor, brocade arm guards, white leg bindings, purple belts, and shoes and socks.

sentences.zh: 驍衛翊衛三隊，服平巾幘、緋繡袍、大口袴、錦螣蛇。

translations.literal: Three companies of Brave Guard attendants wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, and brocade teng snakes.
translations.idiomatic: Three companies of Brave Guard attendants wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, and brocade teng snakes.

sentences.zh: 五輅、副輅、耕根車駕士，服平巾幘、青繡衫、青履襪。

translations.literal: Attendants of the Five Carriages, secondary carriages, and Plough-Root carriage wore plain cloth caps, green embroidered shirts, and green shoes and socks.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants of the Five Carriages, secondary carriages, and Plough-Root carriage wore plain cloth caps, green embroidered shirts, and green shoes and socks.

sentences.zh: 教馬官，服襆頭、紅繡抹額、紫繡衫、白袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Horse-training officials wore turbans, red embroidered forehead bands, purple embroidered shirts, white trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-training officials wore turbans, red embroidered forehead bands, purple embroidered shirts, white trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 掌輦、主輦，服武弁、黃繡衫、紫繡誕帶。

translations.literal: Palanquin handlers and chief palanquin handlers wore military caps, yellow embroidered shirts, and purple embroidered ceremonial sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin handlers and chief palanquin handlers wore military caps, yellow embroidered shirts, and purple embroidered ceremonial sashes.

sentences.zh: 攏禦馬者，服帖金帽、紫繡大袖衫、銀帶。

translations.literal: Imperial horse handlers wore gold-inlaid caps, purple embroidered large-sleeve shirts, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial horse handlers wore gold-inlaid caps, purple embroidered large-sleeve shirts, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 執真武幢者，服武弁、皂繡衫、紫繡誕帶。

translations.literal: True Martial banner-staff bearers wore military caps, black embroidered shirts, and purple embroidered ceremonial sashes.
translations.idiomatic: True Martial banner-staff bearers wore military caps, black embroidered shirts, and purple embroidered ceremonial sashes.

sentences.zh: 五牛旗輿士，服武弁、五色繡衫、大口袴，銀帶。

translations.literal: Five Ox flag litter bearers wore military caps, five-colored embroidered shirts, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Five Ox flag litter bearers wore military caps, five-colored embroidered shirts, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 掩後隊，服黑鍪甲、錦臂鞲、行縢。

translations.literal: Rear-cover company wore black helmet armor, brocade arm guards, and leg bindings.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-cover company wore black helmet armor, brocade arm guards, and leg bindings.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹令、丞，服綠袴褶冠、銀褐裙、金銅革帶、緋白大帶、履襪。

translations.literal: Directors and deputy directors of the music office wore green jacket-and-trousers caps, silver-brown skirts, gold-copper leather belts, scarlet and white great belts, and shoes and socks.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and deputy directors of the music office wore green jacket-and-trousers caps, silver-brown skirts, gold-copper leather belts, scarlet and white great belts, and shoes and socks.

sentences.zh: 太常寺府史、典事、司天令史，服襆頭、綠衫、黃半臂。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices clerks, ritual attendants, and astronomy clerks wore turbans, green shirts, and yellow half-sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices clerks, ritual attendants, and astronomy clerks wore turbans, green shirts, and yellow half-sleeves.

sentences.zh: 太常主帥鞞鼓、金鉦、節鼓人，服平巾幘、緋繡袍、大口袴，抹帶、錦螣蛇；

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices chiefs of frame drums, gongs, and rhythm drums wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, forehead sashes, and brocade teng snakes;
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices chiefs of frame drums, gongs, and rhythm drums wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, wide trousers, forehead sashes, and brocade teng snakes;

sentences.zh: 歌、拱宸管、簫、笳、笛、觱栗，無螣蛇。

translations.literal: singers, Gongchen pipes, xiao, jia, di, and bili had no teng snakes.
translations.idiomatic: Singers and players of Gongchen pipes, xiao, jia, di, and bili had no teng snakes.

sentences.zh: 太常大鼓、長鳴、小鼓、中鳴，服黃雷花袍、袴、抹額、抹帶。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices great drums, long horns, small drums, and middle horns wore yellow thunder-flower robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices great drums, long horns, small drums, and middle horns wore yellow thunder-flower robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.

sentences.zh: 太常鐃、大橫吹，服緋苣文袍、袴、抹額、抹帶。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices nao and great transverse flutes wore scarlet juwen robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices nao and great transverse flutes wore scarlet juwen robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.

sentences.zh: 太常羽葆鼓、小橫吹，服青苣文袍、袴、抹額、抹帶。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices feather-canopy drums and small transverse flutes wore green juwen robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices feather-canopy drums and small transverse flutes wore green juwen robes, trousers, forehead bands, and forehead sashes.

sentences.zh: 排列官、令史、府史，服黑介幘、緋衫、白袴、白勒帛。

translations.literal: Formation officers, clerks, and record keepers wore black kerchiefs, scarlet shirts, white trousers, and white waist sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Formation officers, clerks, and record keepers wore black kerchiefs, scarlet shirts, white trousers, and white waist sashes.

sentences.zh: 司辰、典事、漏刻生，服青袴褶冠、革帶。

translations.literal: Timekeepers, ritual attendants, and clepsydra students wore green jacket-and-trousers caps and leather belts.
translations.idiomatic: Timekeepers, ritual attendants, and clepsydra students wore green jacket-and-trousers caps and leather belts.

sentences.zh: 殿中少監、奉禦、供奉、排列官，引駕仗內排列承直官、大將、金吾引駕、押仗、押旗，服襆頭、紫公服、烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Vice directors of the palace service, attendants, palace attendants, formation officers, leading escort formation officers, great generals, Golden Guard leading escorts, guard officers, and flag officers wore turbans, purple official dress, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors of the palace service, attendants, palace attendants, formation officers, leading escort formation officers, great generals, Golden Guard leading escorts, guard officers, and flag officers wore turbans, purple official dress, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 尚輦奉禦、直長、乘黃令丞、千牛長史、進馬四色官，服襆頭、綠公服、白袴、金銅帶、烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Palanquin attendants, chief attendants, Carriage Yellow office directors, Thousand-Ox chief clerks, and four-color horse-presenting officials wore turbans, green official dress, white trousers, gold-copper belts, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin attendants, chief attendants, Carriage Yellow office directors, Thousand-Ox chief clerks, and four-color horse-presenting officials wore turbans, green official dress, white trousers, gold-copper belts, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 殿中職掌執傘扇人，服襆頭、碧襴、金銅帶、烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Palace attendants in charge of umbrellas and fans wore turbans, jade-green damask, gold-copper belts, and black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants in charge of umbrellas and fans wore turbans, jade-green damask, gold-copper belts, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 〈（舊衣黃，太平興國六年，並內侍省並改服以碧。）〉

translations.literal: (Formerly they wore yellow; in the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, the Inner Palace Service collectively changed dress to jade-green.)
translations.idiomatic: (Formerly they wore yellow robes; in the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, the Inner Palace Service collectively changed to jade-green dress.)

sentences.zh: 凡繡文：金吾衛以辟邪，左右衛以瑞馬，驍衛以雕虎，屯衛以赤豹，武衛以瑞鷹，領軍衛以白澤，監門衛以師子，千牛衛以犀牛，六軍以孔雀，樂工以鸞，耕根車駕士以鳳銜嘉禾，進賢車以瑞麟，明遠車以對鳳，羊車以瑞羊，指南車以孔雀，記裏鼓、黃鉞車以對鵝，白鷺車以翔鷺，鸞旗車以瑞鸞，崇德車以辟邪，皮軒車以虎，屬車以雲鶴，豹尾車以立豹，相風烏輿以烏，五牛旗以五色牛，餘皆以寶相花。

translations.literal: Embroidery patterns in general: Golden Guard used ward-off evil; Left and Right Guards used auspicious horses; Brave Guard used carved tigers; Garrison Guard used red leopards; Martial Guard used auspicious eagles; Army-leading Guard used White Ze; Gate Guard used lions; Thousand-Ox Guard used rhinoceroses; Six Armies used peacocks; musicians used luan; Plough-Root carriage attendants used phoenixes holding auspicious grain; Advance Worthy carriage used auspicious qilin; Bright Distance carriage used paired phoenixes; sheep carriage used auspicious sheep; compass carriage used peacocks; mile-counting drum and yellow battle-axe carriages used paired geese; white egret carriage used flying egrets; luan banner carriage used auspicious luan; Honoring Virtue carriage used ward-off evil; leather-canopied carriage used tigers; attendant carriages used cloud cranes; leopard-tail carriage used standing leopards; wind-measuring bird carriage used birds; Five Ox flags used five-colored oxen; all others used treasure-flower patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidery patterns in general: the Golden Guard used ward-off evil; the Left and Right Guards used auspicious horses; the Brave Guard used carved tigers; the Garrison Guard used red leopards; the Martial Guard used auspicious eagles; the Army-leading Guard used White Ze; the Gate Guard used lions; the Thousand-Ox Guard used rhinoceroses; the Six Armies used peacocks; musicians used luan; Plough-Root carriage attendants used phoenixes holding auspicious grain; the Advance Worthy carriage used auspicious qilin; the Bright Distance carriage used paired phoenixes; the sheep carriage used auspicious sheep; the compass carriage used peacocks; the mile-counting drum and yellow battle-axe carriages used paired geese; the white egret carriage used flying egrets; the luan banner carriage used auspicious luan; the Honoring Virtue carriage used ward-off evil; the leather-canopied carriage used tigers; attendant carriages used cloud cranes; the leopard-tail carriage used standing leopards; the wind-measuring bird carriage used birds; the Five Ox flags used five-colored oxen; and all others used treasure-flower patterns.

sentences.zh: 六引內巾服之製：清道官，服武弁、緋繡衫、革帶。

translations.literal: Regulations for headgear and dress within the Six Guides: Clear Path officials wore military caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, and leather belts.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for headgear and dress within the Six Guides: Clear Path officials wore military caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, and leather belts.

sentences.zh: 持幰弩、車輻棒者，服平巾赤幘、緋繡衫、赤袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of screened crossbows and wheel-spoke clubs wore plain caps with scarlet kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered shirts, scarlet trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of screened crossbows and wheel-spoke clubs wore plain caps with scarlet kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered shirts, scarlet trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 青衣，服平巾青幘、青袴褶。

translations.literal: Blue-robed attendants wore plain caps with green kerchiefs and green jacket-and-trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Blue-robed attendants wore plain caps with green kerchiefs and green jacket-and-trousers.

sentences.zh: 持戟、傘、扇、刀盾者，服黃繡衫、抹額、行縢、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of halberds, umbrellas, fans, and sword-shields wore yellow embroidered shirts, forehead bands, leg bindings, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of halberds, umbrellas, fans, and sword-shields wore yellow embroidered shirts, forehead bands, leg bindings, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 持幡蓋者，服繡衫、抹額、大口袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of pennants and canopies wore embroidered shirts, forehead bands, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of pennants and canopies wore embroidered shirts, forehead bands, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 內告止幡、曲蓋以緋，傳教幡、信幡、絳引幡以黃。

translations.literal: Within, Halt pennants and curved canopies used scarlet; Transmit Edict pennants, Trust pennants, and crimson guide pennants used yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Within, Halt pennants and curved canopies used scarlet. Transmit Edict pennants, Trust pennants, and crimson guide pennants used yellow.

sentences.zh: 執誕馬轡、儀刀、麾、幢、節、夾槊、大角者，服平巾幘、緋繡衫、大口袴、銀帶。

translations.literal: Bearers of ceremonial horse reins, ceremonial swords, command banners, banner-staffs, batons, flanking spears, and great horns wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, wide trousers, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried ceremonial horse reins, ceremonial swords, command banners, banner-staffs, batons, flanking spears, and great horns wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, wide trousers, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿內，執轡，並錦絡衫帽。

translations.literal: Within the grand imperial escort, those holding reins all wore brocade-net shirts and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Within the grand imperial escort, all who held reins wore brocade-net shirts and caps.

sentences.zh: 持弓箭、槊者，服武弁、緋繡衫、白袴。

translations.literal: Bow, arrow, and spear bearers wore military caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, and white trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried bows, arrows, and spears wore military caps, scarlet embroidered shirts, and white trousers.

sentences.zh: 駕士，服錦帽、繡戎服大袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants wore brocade caps, embroidered military-style great robes, and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage attendants wore brocade caps, embroidered military-style great robes, and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 弓箭以青，槊以紫。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows used green; spears used purple.
translations.idiomatic: Bows and arrows were green; spears were purple.

sentences.zh: 持鞞鼓者，服平巾幘、緋繡對鳳袍、大口袴、白抹帶、銀螣蛇。

translations.literal: Frame drum bearers wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered paired-phoenix robes, wide trousers, white forehead sashes, and silver teng snakes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried frame drums wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered paired-phoenix robes, wide trousers, white forehead sashes, and silver teng snakes.

sentences.zh: 鐃吹部內，服平巾幘、緋繡袍、白抹帶、白袴，餘悉同大駕前後部。

translations.literal: Within the nao and wind-instrument section, they wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, white forehead sashes, and white trousers; the rest was all the same as the front and rear sections of the grand procession.
translations.idiomatic: Within the nao and wind-instrument section, they wore plain cloth caps, scarlet embroidered robes, white forehead sashes, and white trousers. The rest was the same as the front and rear sections of the grand procession.

sentences.zh: 其繡衣文：清道以雲鶴，幰弩以辟邪，車輻以白澤，駕士司徒以瑞馬，牧以隼，御史大夫以獬豸，兵部尚書以虎，太常卿以鳳，縣令以雉，樂工以鸞，餘悉以寶相花。

translations.literal: Their embroidered garment patterns: Clear Path used cloud cranes; screened crossbows used ward-off evil; wheel-spoke clubs used White Ze; carriage attendants and the Minister of Education used auspicious horses; the Minister of Pasturage used hawks; the Censor-in-Chief used xiezhi; the Minister of War used tigers; the Minister of Rites used phoenixes; county magistrates used pheasants; musicians used luan; all others used treasure-flower patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Their embroidered garment patterns were as follows: Clear Path used cloud cranes; screened crossbows used ward-off evil; wheel-spoke clubs used White Ze; carriage attendants and the Minister of Education used auspicious horses; the Minister of Pasturage used hawks; the Censor-in-Chief used xiezhi; the Minister of War used tigers; the Minister of Rites used phoenixes; county magistrates used pheasants; musicians used luan; and all others used treasure-flower patterns.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆四年，範質議：按《開元禮》，武官陪立大仗，加螣蛇裲襠，如袖無身，以覆其膊胳，蓋掖下縫也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, Fan Zhi proposed: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, when military officers stood attendance at the great guard formation, they added teng-snake doublets like sleeves without a body to cover the upper arms—it was sewn under the armpit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong, Fan Zhi proposed: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, when military officers stood attendance at the great guard formation, they added teng-snake doublets like sleeves without a body to cover the upper arms, sewn under the armpit.

sentences.zh: 從肩領覆臂膊，共一尺二寸。

translations.literal: From the shoulder and collar it covered the upper arms, totaling one foot two inches.
translations.idiomatic: From the shoulder and collar it covered the upper arms, totaling one foot two inches in length.

sentences.zh: 又按《釋文》、《玉篇》相傳云：其一當胸，其一當背，謂之“兩當”。

translations.literal: Also according to the Exegesis and Jade Chapters, tradition says: one piece covered the chest and one covered the back, called the "double cover."
translations.idiomatic: Also according to the Exegesis and Jade Chapters, tradition says that one piece covered the chest and one covered the back, called the "double cover."

sentences.zh: 今詳裲襠之製，其領連所覆膊胳，其一當左膊，其一當右膊，故謂之“ 起膊”。

translations.literal: Examining the present design of the doublet, its collar connected to the covering of the upper arms; one piece covered the left arm and one covered the right arm, and therefore it was called "raised-arm."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the present design of the doublet, its collar connected to the covering of the upper arms. One piece covered the left arm and one covered the right arm, and therefore it was called "raised-arm."

sentences.zh: 今請兼存兩說擇而用之，造裲襠，用當胸、當背之製。

translations.literal: We now request that both explanations be preserved and one chosen for use in making doublets, using the chest-cover and back-cover design.
translations.idiomatic: We now request that both explanations be preserved and one chosen for use in making doublets, adopting the chest-cover and back-cover design.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，禮製局言：鼓吹令、丞冠，又名“袴褶冠。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, the Ritual Regulations Bureau stated: The cap of the director and deputy director of the music office was also called the "jacket-and-trousers cap."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanhe, the Ritual Regulations Bureau reported: The cap of the director and deputy director of the music office was also called the "jacket-and-trousers cap."

sentences.zh: 今鹵簿既除袴褶，冠名不當仍舊，請依舊記如《三禮圖》“委貌冠”製。

translations.literal: Since the imperial escort has now removed jacket-and-trousers dress, the cap name should not remain as before; we request following the old records, such as the "Wei Mao cap" design in the Illustrations of the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial escort has now removed jacket-and-trousers dress, the cap name should not remain as before. We request following the old records, such as the "Wei Mao cap" design in the Illustrations of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.
